source: Made up for the Kwaai lecturer demo. None of these departments, courses or people exist. Department codes are ones UCT does not use.

courses.title: Introduction to Example Sciences
courses.dp: Attendance at 80% of tutorials and a class mark of at least 40%.
courses.outline: A first course in how examples are gathered, compared and explained. Weekly tutorials practise each week's method.

courses.title: Example Sciences in Practice
courses.assessment: Practical reports 30%, class test 20%, final examination 50%.
courses.outline: Follows EXS1001F with weekly practicals and a short project.

courses.title: Methods in Example Sciences
courses.outline: Second-year methods: design, measurement and reporting.

courses.title: Advanced Example Sciences
courses.outline: A third-year course built around one long project.

courses.title: Introduction to Sample Studies
courses.outline: Reading, arguing and writing about samples and what they stand for.

courses.title: Sample Studies and Society
courses.dp: Attendance at 80% of tutorials and submission of all essays.
courses.outline: How samples shape decisions in public life.

courses.title: Theories of Sampling
courses.outline: Second-year theory, read through original texts.

courses.title: Sample Studies Research Project
courses.outline: A supervised research project of 8,000 words.

courses.title: Practice Engineering Fundamentals
courses.dp: Attendance at 90% of practicals and a class mark of at least 40%.
courses.outline: Statics, units and estimation, with a weekly lab.
courses.entry: At least 70% for NSC Mathematics and Physical Sciences.

courses.title: Drawing and Design for Practice Engineers
courses.outline: Hand and computer drawing, and a small design project.

courses.title: Practice Engineering Mechanics
courses.outline: Dynamics and materials for second-year practice engineers.

courses.title: Practice Engineering Design Project
courses.outline: A team design project with a client brief and three design reviews.

good: Lectures are clear and the notes are excellent. Go to every one.
Explains the hard parts slowly. Consultations are really helpful.
The exam was exactly what we practised in tutorials.
One of the best courses I have done. Would take it again.
mid: Content is fine but the pace picks up after the first test.
Do every past paper. The tutorials are where it clicks.
Decent course, just a lot of work in the last block.
Lectures are a bit dry, but the slides are good for self-study.
low: Tests felt much harder than the tutorial problems. Start early.
Hard to follow in lectures. The textbook carried me.
Heavy workload and strict marking. Ask for help early.

held.body: Honestly the worst course, the lecturer is useless and should not be teaching.
I heard the lecturer marks some students easier than others. Something is going on.
held.flags: Possible allegation (needs proof, so a moderator checks it)
